Bay Area · times verified on each venue’s own page

This Week in the Bay

Tuesday–Sunday, September 1–6, 2026 · Labor Day weekend · SF · East Bay · South Bay · North Bay

A full sweep of the region’s arts calendar. This is a gap week for the big subscription seasons — the Symphony, SFJAZZ, SF Opera, Cal Performances and most dance companies all open the following weekend — so the sweep went wider instead: an experimental-film festival, a circus tent in Alameda, a theater company giving its final performance ever, free telescopes, and a fire dragon in Chinatown. Use Day and Region to narrow.

🎞️ CROSSROADS 2026 — 8 experimental programs, Fri–Sun 🎪 The Soiled Dove big top, w/ Joan Baez 🎭 Central Works’ last-ever show 🔭 Free telescope nights Fri & Sat 🏮 Hungry Ghost Festival, Chinatown

The Top 5 This Week

Five picks across all categories — chosen for rarity, variety and things that genuinely will not happen again.
01 · EXPERIMENTAL FILM

JG Thirlwell scores Harry Smith’s “Heaven and Earth Magic”

Fri Sep 4, 9:30pm · Gray Area, Mission, SF · $20/$15

The industrial-noise composer performs a live surround-sound score — electronics, triggered samples, theremin — to the beatnik mystic’s obsessively occult 1957–62 stop-motion film. One night, and nothing else this year comes close.

02 · IMMERSIVE CIRCUS

The Soiled Dove — under the big top

Fri Sep 4 & Sat Sep 5, 7:30pm dinner / 9pm show · Alameda Point · from $75

Vau de Vire’s Barbary-Coast dinner-circus inside a 12,000 sq ft Italian tent on a decommissioned naval airfield — aerialists over your table, and Joan Baez in the 2026 cast.

03 · THEATER · ★ SF CHRONICLE

Central Works: “The Prince,” Parts 1 & 2

Thu Sep 3–Sun Sep 6 · Berkeley City Club · $20–$45 sliding

Gary Graves’ six-act Machiavelli epic, begun in grad school in 1986 — and world premieres #80 and #81 for a company that closes forever when the curtain falls Sunday. Thursday is pay-what-you-can.

04 · LITERARY

SF Zine Fest, 25th Annual — with V. Vale

Sun Sep 6, 11am–5pm · The Hibernia, 1 Jones St, SF · FREE

210+ exhibitors of zines and small-press comics in a restored 1892 bank — plus a Q&A with V. Vale of RE/Search, the man who documented punk from the inside, joined by Penelope Houston of The Avengers.

05 · STREET RITUAL

Chinatown Hungry Ghost Festival

Sat Sep 5, 2–6pm, burn after dark · Portsmouth Square, SF · FREE

The gates of the underworld open: free peace buns, ancestor altars, fortune sticks — then a straw Ghost King studded with ten thousand lit sticks of incense processed through the streets to carry away misfortune.

✦ 1883 & 1916 refractors
ObservatoryFri & Sat 7:30–10:30

Chabot Free Telescope Viewings

Chabot Space & Science · Oakland Hills · East Bay
FREE · clear skies only

Three historic domes 1,500 ft above the Bay: “Leah” (8″ Alvan Clark, 1883), “Rachel” (20″, 1916 — the largest refractor in the West open to the public) and “Nellie.” Forecast is partly cloudy both nights; check the humidity webcam before you drive up.

Foothill Observatory — stars, then sun

Repertory Cinema

14 films

An exceptional week on celluloid: a newly struck 35mm print, 70mm at the restored Castro, 3-D on 35mm, four 4K restorations at BAMPFA, three live-scored silents, and an eight-program experimental festival. Routine first-runs omitted.

Theater

9 shows

An unusually strong theater week: two once-ever closings, a major regional opening, and three free outdoor productions. A.C.T., Shotgun, Magic and The Marsh are all dark.

👑
TOP PICK★ Chronicle✦ Company’s last-ever show
World PremiereThu–Sat 7pm · Sun 5pm

The Prince, Parts 1 & 2 — Central Works

Berkeley City Club · 2315 Durant Ave · East Bay
$35–45 · Thu pay-what-you-can · day-of sliding $20–45

Gary Graves’ six-act pair on Machiavelli — Part 1 is young Niccolò against Savonarola and Cesare Borgia; Part 2 brings in Leonardo, Michelangelo and a farcical poisoning plot. He has been writing it since 1986. These are world premieres #80 and #81, and the final production of the company’s 36th and last season — Sunday is the last performance Central Works will ever give. Parts alternate nightly; call 510.558.1381 to check which plays when.

How this was built

Every source row in sources.md was scanned across fifteen parallel sweeps — aggregators, museums, galleries, literary, immersive, oddities, lectures, classical, theater, cinema, dance, markets, cultural centers, casual/spa and critics’ outlets — then filtered against the taste profile and ranked by hand. Times were read off each venue’s own event page rather than an aggregator grid wherever one existed.

Verify before you go

Chabot and Foothill telescope nights are clear-sky-only. Forecasts were good for Fri and Sat, but Chabot closes its historic refractors above 90% humidity — check their weather station the same evening. Central Works alternates Part 1 and Part 2 nightly and publishes the grid only as an image; call 510.558.1381. JCCCNC does not publish times or prices anywhere readable — phone (415) 567-5505. Computer History Museum demo times aren’t online; call ahead. Two BAMPFA Alice Diop screenings (Thu, Fri) are sold out. Robert Reich is sold out in person; online tickets remain.

Deliberately left out

EDM and DJ club nights, arena shows (J. Cole at Oakland Arena, Diana Ross and Babyface in Napa), sports, bar crawls, brunch-as-event, networking mixers and expos — including the touring Oddities & Curiosities Expo, which reads well but is an expo. Pride- and identity-framed programming was deprioritized rather than removed; a few items are noted in passing where the work itself was on-taste.

Just missed the window

Almost everything big opens the following weekend: SFJAZZ (Sep 10), Smuin’s season opener (Sep 11), SF Opera’s Simon Boccanegra (Sep 12), Bach Dancing & Dynamite (Sep 13), Flower Piano in the Botanical Garden (Sep 10–20), Audium’s new run (Sep 11), Hosfelt and Jessica Silverman openings (Sep 10), Bay Area Theatre Week (Sep 10–20), the Haight St Fair (Sep 20), and Hubba Hubba Revue’s 20th anniversary (Sep 20). Worth booking now.
